label: text
text: MINERS SUMMONED

label: paragraph_title
text: Rugby, Sept. 16.

label: text
text: The Prime Minister, who returned from Aix, les Bains last night, had a long consultation with the members of the Coal Committee of the Cabinet this morning.

label: text
text: In the afternoon there was a meeting of the full Cabinet, lasting two hours. It is understood that the Cabinet considered the whole inspection of the dispute in the coal industry, and endorsed the action taken by the Cabinet.

label: text
text: The Prime Minister has "summoned the miners' officials to move him at Downing Street to-morrow morning, at 10 o'clock and he will also to-morrow see the President of the Conf Owners' Association.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: Pending the Government's action in the coal dispute the drift back of miners to work continues. The mine owners estimate that, including safety men and outcroppers, at least 150,000 men are now employed and half a million tons of coal are being produced weekly.

label: paragraph_title
text: HOUSE ENTERED THROUGH SKYLIGHT.

label: text
text: PROPERTY STOLEN.

label: text
text: A skylight which was left open provided access to a thief early this morning at No. 292, Des Vœux Road (Central), occupied by a Chinese married woman.

label: text
text: The thief made his exit the same way after taking a leather bag which contained the woman's jewellery and clothing. Discarding the bag and some of the contents which did not prove valuable, the intruder got away with property valued at $17.1 and an American passport.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: POSITION OF TYPHQON OBSCURE.

label: text
text: The Observatory reports to-day as under:—

label: text
text: Pressure has increased moderately over Formosa and slightly at the majority of other, reporting stations.

label: text
text: In the absence of observations from the Japanese Empire no position can be assigned to the typhoon.

label: text
text:
There appears to be a shallow depression over Indo-China, and an anticyclone over S.E. Mongolia.
Forecast till noon tomorrow: East winds moderate: fine to cloudy.

label: text
text: The gross cash receipts from sales of opium in the Colony last year totalled $14,541,757 the net revenue, excluding $72,438 derived from opium licence fees, being $12,476,028. Increased sales resulted from the influx of labour during the latter half of the year in consequence of improved conditions in the rubber market and the general atmosphere of prosperity. All the raw opium imported was Indian opium.

label: paragraph_title
text: AMERICAN KILLED:

label: paragraph_title
text: OUTRAGE BY FLEEING BANDITS.

label: text
text: SOLDIERS SHOOT TWO:

label: text
text: Mexico City, Sept. 16..

label: text
text: Mr. Rosenthal was murdered by the bandits when Federal soldiers were pursuing them so close that they were able to kill two of the bandits.

label: text
text: It appears that "a ransom of $10,000 had been demanded for Mr. Rosenthal's release.—Reuter's American Service.

label: text
text: [A cable from Mexico City on September 13 stated:—Federal soldiers are pursuing bandits who are holding as prisoner Mr. Jacob Rosenthal, a retired New York merchant, after holding up a car in which he was motoring with a party (including three other Americans) 40 miles from Mexico City as the party was returning from the seaside resort of Cuernavaca. The bandits levelled their rifles, ordered the car to stop, took all the money and jewels, seized Rosenthal and dragged him into the neighbouring woods. The curious fact is that no ransom is demanded, and the authorities are puzzled to know why Rosenthal was specially selected as prisoner.]

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: METAL UP £60.

label: text
text: Rugby, Sept. 16.

label: text
text: There is a small boom in tim shares on the Stock Exchange as the result of the rising price of tin, which to-day touched £316.12.6 per ton for cash.

label: text
text: Tin has gone up about £60 per ton for cash. Its unusual price is due to the increasing shortage in the floating supply owing to the consumption being greater than the production.—British Wireless Service.

text: LATEST INFORMATION

label: text
text: From Australia and Manila the steamer "Aki Maru" arrived yesterday afternoon with passengers for Hong Kong. She brought about 500 tons of general cargo besides Australian and Manila mail. The "Aki Maru" will sail for Japan this afternoon with passengers and cargo.

label: text
text: Messrs. Mackinnon, Mackenzie & Co. announces that their steamer "Kidderpore" left Singapore for this port yesterday morning and is due here on September 20 at daylight with passengers, cargo and European mail.

label: text
text: Two B. & S. steamers arrived this morning. The "Kalgan" from Bangkok, with steerage passengers and about 300 tons of general cargo, and the s.s. "Telemachus" from Shanghai via Han-kow, with passengers and mail.

label: text
text: Bound for Australia and Manila the s.s. "Taiping" of the Australian and Oriental line sailed this morning with passengers, over 800 tons of general cargo and mail for Manila and Australia.

label: text
text: To-morrow at noon, the s.s. "Malwa" of the P. & O. line will sail for Europe, via Marseilles, with passengers, cargo and mail. The "Malwa" arrived this morning from Yokohama via ports with through passengers, cargo and Siberian mail for Hong Kong.

label: text
text: The Bank Line, Ltd., has added "to its service the steamers "City of Baroda' and the "City of Cairo" which will be running between Hong Kong and New York via the Philippines, Colombo and the Suez Canal. Both steamers are equipped with first and second class accommodations, fare for first class being £100 and for the second class will be furnished on application at the local office of the Bank Line, Ltd.

label: text
text: To reload at San Pedro, California, the oil tanker of the Standard Oil Co. s.s. "Levant Arrow" left for that port yesterday afternoon, via Shanghai.

label: paragraph_title
text: Pilots on Strike.

label: text
text: According to a Wanhsien telegram of yesterday's date, General Yang Sen has concentrated his troops as well as cannon near Hungshachi in order to prepare for the reported fresh British expedition, and 70 per cent. of the citizens have fled and almost all houses are closed.

label: text
text: The same telegram also states that owing to the reports that General Lu Chin-shan will mediate between General Yang Sen's troops and the British war vessels and that Chinese pilots have gone on strike against British steamers, the excitement of the citizens there has been alleviated.—“Toho.”

label: text
text: Anti-British Agitation.

label: text
text: The Chinese are firing on all foreign vessels entering Hapkow reports the Shanghai correspondent of the London "Daily Mail." "A British gunboat was reported to have been hit but the damage could not be ascertained by the correspondent.

label: text
text: Meanwhile Peking reports that the British are leaving Szechuan province because of the anti-foreign feeling there. (Szechuan is west of Hupeh, the province in which Hankow is situated. Trouble at Wanhsien recently caused a stir in Szechuan). The Chinese are growing dangerous and the lives of white residents are believed to be in considerable danger.—" United Press.

label: paragraph_title
text: Tension Relieved.

label: paragraph_title
text: Peking, Sept. 13.

label: text
text: It is thought that General Yang Sen will be left to nurse his own troubles. Thus with hostility behind and front there is a general expectation that he will soon brought to heel.

label: text
text: The tension concerning the position in Szechuan has been considerably relieved by the further news that the local generals are very much shaken by fears of British reprisals.

label: text
text: No news has been received as yet of the Navy's plans, but it is reported from Hankow that the Consuls's representations, to the belligerents have had the effect of ensuring a cessation of the indiscriminate firing on British ships.—“N.-C. Daily News.”

label: paragraph_title
text: AMERICAN REPORTS

label: paragraph_title
text: Admiral Sends Message to Navy Department.

label: text
text: The Destroyers “Pope” and “Stewart,” at present stationed at Hankow, are being relieved by the Destroyers “Ford” and “Pillsbury,” now at Chefoo. The “Pope” will participate in target practice at Chefoo and the “Stewart” will proceed to Manila for overhauling.—“United Press.”

label: text
text: Admiral: Clarence B. Williams, commander-in-chief of the American Asiatic Fleet, sent a message to the Navy Department to day confirming the report that the American destroyers "Stewart" and "Pope" were fired upon in Chinese waters on September 5. He also added that the American steam "ling" was fired on the day before.

label: text
text:
Culprits Not Identified.
Admiral Williams' message said that two men aboard the destroyers received "surface wounds," and that the vessels were struck several times.

label: text
text: The firing came from the south side of the Yangtze River 50 miles below Hankow and was not returned, as the destroyers were unable to locate the source of the shell. The firing on the steamer "Iling" was described as heavy and occurred five miles below Hankow.

label: text
text: A second cablegram from Admiral Williams dated yesterday said that the American gunboat "Palos," the destroyer "Stewart" and the mine-sweeper "Pigeon," defended themselves after being heavily bombardied with rifle and artillery fire by unidentified forces near Hankow. There were no casualties.—"Associated Press."
